pmc-12490442.title: CHANGES IN PRE-AND POST-INTERVENTION HAND HYGIENE COMPLIANCE IN ICU ON WHO HANDWASHING POSTERS
pmc-12490442.creator: Lada Lijović, Josip Jaman, Yannick Mudrovčić, Dominik Ivanković, Katarina Jelić, Lana Videc Penavić, Tomislav Radočaj, Hrvoje Silovski
pmc-12490442.description: SUMMARYHealthcare-associated infections (HAI) cause more deaths in the European Union than all other infectious diseases. Hand hygiene (HH) has been considered the most important means of preventing HAIs but HH compliance is generally less than 50%. One of the five steps that the World Health Organization (WHO) guidelines identify to be specifically implemented are poster reminders.

pmc-12733066.title: SpyTagged Mimotope Peptide Mediated Competitive Antigen-Based Rapid Quantitative Immunoassays for Uniconazole Residue
pmc-12733066.creator: Tailong Wei, Xiao Chen, Chong Cai, Yuanzhen Guo, Mengjun Zhou, Qiannan Gao, Qinghua He
pmc-12733066.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Mimotope-based immunoassays offer an eco-friendly alternative to chemically synthesized antigens for the quantitative analysis of small molecules, but their use for practical on-site and high-throughput residue monitoring remains limited. Herein, we report the selection, production, and application of a phage display–derived mimotope targeting an anti-uniconazole monoclonal antibody (UCZ-mAb), with the aim of developing two complementary immunoassays that enable sensitive, eco-friendly detection of UCZ residues in agricultural samples.

pmc-12971787.title: Time-Restricted Eating, Cardiometabolic Health in Obesity and The Optimal Length of the Eating Window
pmc-12971787.creator: Bianca Monteiro Silva, Gabriela Geraldo Benzoni, Marcela Coffacci de Lima Viliod, Caroline Fogagnolo, Gabriela Ferreira Abud, Gabriela Ueta Ortiz, Ivo Vieira de Sousa Neto, Ana Cláudia Rossini-Venturini, Sofia Germano Travieso, Ellen Cristini de Freitas
pmc-12971787.description: Purpose of ReviewThis narrative review aims to evaluate how the duration of eating windows influences the cardiometabolic effects of Time-Restricted Eating (TRE) protocols among individuals with obesity. In the context of the global obesity epidemic, TRE has emerged as a promising dietary approach, alternative to conventional energy restriction, capable of improving cardiometabolic health by aligning food intake with circadian rhythms.

pmc-13006822.title: POLQ promotes tumor progression and immunosuppression via ATM-P53 signaling in endometrial cancer
pmc-13006822.creator: Ningning Zhu, Juanjuan Wang, Xiaoli Zhang, Kai Tang, Lei Gong, Yi Hu
pmc-13006822.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Endometrial cancer (EC) is a one of the most prevalent gynecological malignancies worldwide; however, the molecular mechanisms driving its progression remain insufficiently understood. In the present study, DNA polymerase θ (POLQ), which is implicated in multiple types of cancer, was comprehensively investigated in EC using data from The Cancer Genome Atlas and TNMplot datasets, with further validation in an independent patient cohort. POLQ expression was markedly upregulated in EC tissues and was associated with reduced 15-year overall survival.

pmc-13067063.title: Engineering of the Melanoma Inhibitor of Apoptosis (ML‐IAP) Anticancer Peptide Through Comprehensive In Silico Approaches
pmc-13067063.creator: Haitham Ahmed Al-Madhagi, Muhammad shahab, Zheng Guojun, Gamil Al-Madhagy, Mohammed Bourhia, Gamal A. Shazly, Musaab Dauelbait, Zunnan Huang
pmc-13067063.description: Background and AimsMelanoma represents the most malignant type of skin cancer. It is estimated that approximately 100,000 new cases of melanoma were diagnosed in 2022, resulting in over 7600 deaths in the United States alone. Recently, anticancer peptides (ACPs) have emerged as novel therapeutic agents for cancer, offering higher potency, biocompatibility, and fewer adverse reactions in host cells.

pmc-13115436.title: Enhancing Stability of Vitamin-Fortified Protein Beverages: Optimization of Stabilizer Type and Concentration and Screening of Natural Antioxidant Combinations
pmc-13115436.creator: Jiaxin Li, Sumei Ru, Linru Zhu, Yingshuang Lu, Junping Wang, Yan Zhang, Lu Dong, Shuo Wang
pmc-13115436.description: This study optimized stabilizer type and concentration, and screened natural antioxidant combinations to enhance the stability of a protein beverage fortified with vitamins A, D2, and D3. Three stabilizers—carrageenan, sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (Na-CMC), and microcrystalline cellulose (MCC)—were evaluated at 0.15–0.45% (w/v) during accelerated storage at 45 °C for 21 days.

pmc-13148269.title: Computed Tomography Diagnostic Reference Levels Worldwide and in Jordan: Implications for Patient Dose Reduction
pmc-13148269.creator: Ammar A Oglat, Suhaib Shdaifat, Mohannad Adel Sayah, Ahmed Abukonna, Wadah M Ali Khogali
pmc-13148269.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Computed tomography (CT) contributes substantially to medical radiation exposure, making diagnostic reference levels (DRLs) essential for dose optimization and patient protection. This narrative review summarizes international CT DRL practices and examines the current status of DRL development in Jordan. Published studies and key guidance documents addressing adult and pediatric CT DRLs, including CTDIvol, dose-length product (DLP), and size-specific dose estimate (SSDE) where available, were reviewed to identify common implementation approaches, frequently used dose metrics, and evidence gaps relevant to Jordan.

pmc-13221917.title: Trabecular Bone Score and Bone Turnover Markers Unmask Early Skeletal Fragility in Children and Adolescents With Type 1 Diabetes
pmc-13221917.creator: Vinod Ullatil, Piyas Gargari, Mainak Banerjee, Pradip Mukhopadhyay, Sujoy Ghosh
pmc-13221917.description: BackgroundCompromised bone health is a recognized consequence of type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM), particularly in adults. Studies that comprehensively assess dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry parameters, trabecular bone score (TBS), and bone turnover markers (BTMs) are scarce in children and adolescents with T1DM.

pmc-13277631.title: Impact of lactic acid bacterial strain and storage temperature on the quality and functionality of fermented mulberry juice
pmc-13277631.creator: Yuanxia Wang, Sixian Tan, Tianhang Wang, Dejian Huang, Pingkang Xu
pmc-13277631.description: This study systematically analyzes the differences in quality parameters and volatile flavor compounds of mulberry juice fermented with Lactobacillus plantarum (LPJ) and Lactobacillus delbrueckii subsp. bulgaricus (LBJ) during storage at room temperature (25 °C) and 4 °C. Lactic acid fermentation reduced sugar content, pH, and protein levels.

pmc-13421612.creator: Rachel Pereur, Yvan Marc, Yuliya Lim, Alain Schmitt, Marilyne Malbouyres, Anatole Chessel, Florence Ruggiero, Marie-Claire Schanne-Klein, Laurence Legeai-Mallet, Emilie Dambroise

pmc-13540720.title: Spinal epidural calcified chondroid mesenchymal neoplasm mimicking epidural abscess: a case report
pmc-13540720.creator: Joshua Estin, Dev Patel, Lawrence Kenyon, Islam Fayed, Karthik Madhavan
pmc-13540720.description: Calcified chondroid mesenchymal neoplasm (CCMN) is a rare chondroid matrix-producing tumour characterized by distinctive histopathology and recurrent FN1-receptor tyrosine kinase gene fusions. Reported cases have predominantly involved the distal extremities and temporomandibular joint, with no previously reported spinal cases. We present the first reported spinal epidural lesion morphologically consistent with CCMN.

pmc-13644589.title: Gut bacteria and their metabolites may influence our decisions, intelligence, cognition, and consciousness
pmc-13644589.creator: Leon M T Dicks, Alfred Botha, Carolina Pohl
pmc-13644589.description: The human gut hosts approximately 38 trillion bacteria, representing 400 to 500 species. Gut bacteria are in constant communication with the central nervous system (CNS) via the enteric nervous system (ENS), the peripheral nervous system (PNS), the autonomic nervous system (ANS), the immune system, the enteroendocrine system (EES), and the vagus nerve (VN).

uslaw-usc-t38-s7622.description: United States Code, Title 38 (Veterans’ Benefits); Part V (Boards, Administrations, And Services); Chapter 76 (Health Professionals Educational Assistance Program); Subchapter III (Tuition Reimbursement Program). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) To be eligible to participate in the Tuition Reimbursement Program, an individual must be a full-time employee in the Department permanently assigned to a Department health-care facility and must be enrolled.

uslaw-usc-t5-s5527.title: 5 U.S.C. § 5527 — Regulations
uslaw-usc-t5-s5527.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t5-s5527.description: United States Code, Title 5 (Government Organization And Employees); Part III (Employees); Subpart D (Pay And Allowances); Chapter 55 (Pay Administration); Subchapter III (Advancement, Allotment, And Assignment Of Pay). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) To the extent practicable in the public interest, the President shall coordinate the policies and procedures of the respective Executive agencies under this subchapter. (b) The President.
